newsitem.title: USA: Fleming says sets $1.35 bln finance program.
newsitem.headline: Fleming says sets $1.35 bln finance program.

text.p: Fleming Cos Inc said Monday its board approved a $1.35 billion recapitalization program.
The company said it expects the program will result in an extraordinary charge of about $13 million, or $0.35 per share for the second quarter ending July 12.
Fleming said it will use proceeds from the program to repay all outstanding bank debt and retire its floating rate senior notes due 2001.
Fleming said most of the charge represents a non-cash write-off of unamortized financing costs related to the debt to be repaid.

The company said the program consists of an $850 million senior secured credit facility, with bank credit commitments of up to seven years, and $500 million of privately placed senior subordinated notes, with maturities of up to 10 years.

The $850 million senior secured credit facility is comprised of a $600 million revolving credit facility which matures in six years, and a $250 million amortizing term loan which has a final maturity of seven years.

The new bank credit facility will be led by Chase Manhattan Bank as administrative agent. Bank of America NT&SA has been named syndication agent and Societe Generale has been named documentation agent.
The new bank credit facility will replace the company's credit agreement implemented in July 1994 to finance the Scrivner acquisition.
Fleming is a food marketing and distribution company.
